insights: Most trips follow one dominant river-crossing route, while a smaller alternative becomes more common during busy daytime periods.
Speeds decline most near the river crossing during late-afternoon trips, while approach segments on either side remain less variable.
Rainy trips show a larger speed reduction near the river crossing than on comparable urban approach segments.
A small group of late-night trips uses the longer crossing alternative despite otherwise low corridor activity.
summary: A central crossing carries most trips, while the much longer alternative gains share in busy daytime periods and still appears among a small late-night group. Segment data localize late-afternoon and rainy slowdowns at the river crossing.
